rules.title: Ronald V. Dellums Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance - Criminal History Ban
rules.quote: The Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance prohibits rental housing providers in Berkeley from asking about and using criminal history and/or criminal background checks in their rental housing advertising, applications, tenant selection process, or decision-making.
rules.summary: Landlords in Berkeley are prohibited from asking about or using criminal history in advertising, applications, tenant selection, or decision-making.
rules.effective_date_evidence: On April 14, 2020, Berkeley City Council passed the Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance (BMC 13.106).
rules.coverage_text: Exemptions include: lifetime sex offenders; public housing/Section 8 properties (limited); owner-occupied properties (1-3 units) where owner resides as primary residence; units under rental agreement allowing owners to move back; units with existing tenants seeking to sublet or add/replace roommates.
rules.exemption_note: Owner-occupied properties between 1-3 units where owner of record resides in one unit as primary residence are exempt. Lifetime sex offenders exempt. Limited exemptions for public housing/Section 8.
rules.penalty: Administrative fines of at least $1,000 and up to $10,000 per violation, civil damages including actual damages or three times the amount of one month's rent, punitive damages, attorneys' fees and costs, and injunctive relief.

rules.title: Fair Chance Access to Housing - Security Deposit Protection
rules.quote: It is unlawful to do any of the following with regard to current or prospective tenants: Demand a higher security deposit or rental amount based on criminal history
rules.summary: Landlords cannot demand a higher security deposit based on criminal history.
